name: Yala National Park
description: Sri Lanka's most famous national park, renowned for having one of the highest leopard densities in the world, alongside elephants, sloth bears, and diverse bird species.

name: Udawalawe National Park
description: An important habitat for Sri Lankan elephants, this national park offers unparalleled opportunities to observe herds roaming freely around its vast reservoir.

name: Wilpattu National Park
description: Sri Lanka's largest national park, characterized by a unique network of natural sand-rimmed water basins (Villus) and a pristine, wild leopard population.

name: Minneriya National Park
description: Famous for 'The Gathering'—the largest seasonal congregation of Asian elephants in the world, taking place along the dry grassy banks of the Minneriya tank.

name: Kaudulla National Park
description: A key elephant corridor park adjacent to Minneriya, home to dense woods, grasslands, and vast herds of wild elephants.

name: Sinharaja Forest Reserve
description: A UNESCO World Heritage primary tropical rainforest, boasting remarkable biodiversity with endemic birds, trees, amphibians, and reptiles.

name: Horton Plains National Park
description: A protected cloud forest highland plateau featuring rolling grasslands, dramatic cliffs like World's End, montane forest ecosystems, and sambar deer.

name: Bundala National Park
description: An internationally acclaimed RAMSAR wetland site that serves as a wintering ground for thousands of migratory waterfowl, including greater flamingos.

name: Wasgamuwa National Park
description: A pristine sanctuary located along the Mahaweli River, famous for large herds of wild elephants, sloth bears, marsh crocodiles, and ancient ruins.

name: Kumana National Park
description: Renowned for its natural mangrove swamp lake (Kumana Villu), this eastern park is one of Sri Lanka's most significant bird nesting and breeding grounds.

name: Gal Oya National Park
description: A unique wildlife sanctuary centered around the Senanayake Samudraya, famous for boat safaris where wild elephants can be seen swimming between islands.

name: Pigeon Island National Park
description: One of Sri Lanka's two marine national parks, containing pristine coral reefs, blacktip reef sharks, sea turtles, and colorful tropical fish.

name: Knuckles Conservation Forest
description: A rugged UNESCO World Heritage mountain range named for its fist-like peaks, featuring rich cloud forest trails, endemic species, and mountain streams.

name: Royal Botanical Gardens, Peradeniya
description: Sri Lanka's premier 147-acre botanical garden, housing over 4,000 plant species including giant bamboo, royal palms, and a famed orchid house.

name: Hakgala Botanical Garden
description: The second largest botanical garden in Sri Lanka, nestled under the Hakgala Rock, famous for cold-climate roses, ferns, and subtropical flora.

name: Seetawaka Wet Zone Botanical Garden
description: A modern botanical garden in Avissawella dedicated to conserving wet-zone rainforest flora, featuring scenic lakes, glasshouses, and manicured lawns.

name: Mirijjawila Dry Zone Botanical Garden
description: Sri Lanka's first dry-zone botanical garden, focusing on preserving arid-climate plants, herbal vegetation, and native dry-forest trees.

name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka (Dehiwala Zoo)
description: One of the oldest zoos in Asia, housing an extensive collection of indigenous and exotic mammals, birds, reptiles, and a walk-through aquarium.

name: Ridigama Safari Park
description: Sri Lanka's first open-concept safari park, spanning 500 acres where visitors take guided bus tours through open drive-thru animal enclosures.

name: Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage
description: A famous captive breeding and conservation facility for orphaned wild Asian elephants, popular for witnessing daily herd baths in the Ma Oya river.

name: Udawalawe Elephant Transit Home (ETH)
description: A conservation facility supported by Born Free Foundation that rehabilitates orphaned elephant calves before re-releasing them into Udawalawe National Park.

name: Muthurajawela Wetland Sanctuary
description: A coastal brackish marsh ecosystem offering boat safaris to spot water monitor lizards, kingfishers, egrets, and estuarine crocodiles.

name: Water World Kelaniya & Bird Park
description: Sri Lanka's premier public aquatic park featuring over 500 species of marine and freshwater fish, South Asia's first underwater tunnel, and an adjacent exotic bird park.

name: Birds Park Hambantota
description: One of Asia's largest bird parks and research centers, spanning 35 acres with over 3,200 exotic and endemic birds across five dedicated ecological walk-through aviaries.

name: Kosgoda Sea Turtle Conservation Project
description: A pioneering marine sanctuary and hatchery dedicated to protecting endangered sea turtle species, featuring observation tanks for rescued marine turtles and hatchlings.

name: Bentota Turtle Hatchery & Marine Center
description: A coastal marine life conservation center along the southwest beach strip providing shelter, medical care, and release programs for sea turtles.

name: Kalametiya Bird Sanctuary
description: Sri Lanka's oldest coastal wetland bird sanctuary, home to over 150 species of resident and migratory water birds best explored via guided boat safari.

name: Attidiya Bird Sanctuary
description: An urban wetland biodiversity park situated in the Colombo suburbs, offering scenic boardwalk trails for observing indigenous marshland bird species.

name: Anawilundawa Wetland Sanctuary
description: A RAMSAR wetland complex comprising seven ancient man-made tanks, serving as a critical breeding ground and refuge for coastal migratory birds.
